## Wallet UI verification

Compared `f414a7ac` with its merge-base `94d205a3` (main). Each platform used one environment and one fixture for both builds.

### Routing

- Android: captured. The mint removal path changed in `CdkWalletGatewayImpl` and `WalletMessages`, and the result shows on the Mints list.
- iOS: captured. The mint removal path changed in `MintService` and `WalletErrors`, and the result shows on the Mints list.

### Capture environments

- iOS 27.0 (24A434), iPhone 18 Pro simulator, 1206×2622 px, dark, en-US, Dynamic Type Large, Xcode 27.1 (27A9275), status bar fixed at 9:41.
- Android 17 / API 37 (CE2A.260420.019, google_apis arm64-v8a), Pixel 6 profile (Gradle managed device), 1080×2400 px at 420 dpi, dark, en-US, font scale 1.0, System UI demo mode.

### Visual findings

- Both platforms, before: confirming removal of a mint with sat and usd wallets shows "This mint uses multiple currency units and cannot be removed safely yet…". The mint stays listed.
- Both platforms, after: the same action removes the mint. No error is shown, and the remaining mint stays the default.
- Control: the Mints list before removal has no visual delta. The iOS pair is byte-identical. The Android pair is pixel-identical below the status bar; only status-bar icons differ between the two emulator boots.

### iOS — Mints list after confirming removal of a multi-unit mint

</details>

Fixture disclosure: on iOS, the real CDK app talks to local Nutshell (sat) and CDK FakeWallet (sat + usd) test mints. The wallet was onboarded through the UI and relaunched, which makes CDK register the CDK mint's usd wallet. On Android, the instrumentation fake wallet gateway provides `mint.test` (sat) and `second.test` (sat + usd). Removal is triggered from the list: swipe → Remove on iOS, long-press → Remove on Android, then confirm. No real wallet data, balances, or mints are shown.

Limitations: screenshots show the visible result only. That proofs stay in the database is established by CDK's `remove_wallet` source and covered by the unit and UI tests listed in the PR description.

Implementation direction from the CDK reuse review: CDK 0.18.2 already exports `parse_bip321_payment_instruction` through UniFFI (`parseBip321PaymentInstruction` in the generated binding). This existing issue can track replacing the wallet's custom Bitcoin URI extraction on both iOS and Android.

The current helpers extract `creq` and `lightning`/`lightninginvoice`, but do not extract `lno`. Use CDK's structured parsed result while keeping the app's payment-method preference and user confirmation policy explicit. Check legacy input compatibility before removing the custom path.

Suggested validation: unified URIs containing Cashu/BOLT11/BOLT12/on-chain options, `lno`, network mismatch and malformed inputs, existing legacy aliases, and consistent payment selection on both platforms. Standalone Bitcoin-address validation may need a separate helper; do not assume the URI API is a drop-in replacement for every address predicate.

[CDK 0.18.2 FFI API](https://github.com/cashubtc/cdk/blob/v0.18.2/crates/cdk-ffi/src/bip321.rs#L68-L78)

Upstream check completed: cashubtc/cdk#2720 now tracks the structured-error gap relevant to this migration.

`meltLightningAddressQuote` is exported already, but LNURL errors are stringified as `LightningAddressRequest` before FFI, and the FFI conversion reduces many failures to code 50000 plus a message. Distinguishing a missing recipient endpoint, recipient HTTP 502, and mint HTTP 502 without message matching therefore needs upstream error-contract work. This is not a missing resolution API.

The wallet can still improve its current resolver's error presentation independently. Do not silently change fallback behavior when switching to CDK, or treat transport retryability as safe payment retry.

Upstream follow-up after inspecting CDK 0.18.2 and main:

- cashubtc/cdk#2720: new general issue for preserving structured error kinds, source context, and HTTP status. This affects the full error/fallback requirements in #407; it does not block adopting the existing NIP-44 or inbox APIs.
- cashubtc/cdk#2719: existing issue owns clearer melt recovery outcomes and reservation semantics; updated with the FFI relationship rather than creating a duplicate.
- cashubtc/cdk#2479: open wallet/FFI redesign overlaps this API work and should be coordinated with.
- cashubtc/cdk#2639: the authoritative persisted quote-state return fix has already merged upstream. The exact merge commit is not an ancestor of v0.18.2 (the histories have diverged), so check release/backport availability and behavior before removing wallet reload safeguards; no new issue needed for that proposal.

No new FFI exports were identified as prerequisites for #409, #410, or the URI parser integration in #118. Their compatibility and lifecycle tests remain necessary.

[PR #336](https://github.com/cashubtc/wallet/pull/336) removed the problematic lookup of wallets based on advertised currency units. Background sweeps switched to wallets actually registered in CDK.
[PR #334](https://github.com/cashubtc/wallet/pull/334) subsequently changed mint-quote polling to scan persisted quotes directly. Adding a SAT-only mint no longer schedules a speculative USD lookup.
Current melt polling also uses registered wallets.

# Wallet UI verification — failure X and muted amount

- Target: [cashubtc/wallet #413](https://github.com/cashubtc/wallet/pull/413)
- Base: main; actual merge-base `338b0c7397fcc783826222152b6681c9f42bfd7e`
- After: `8d6521879de43c4a641130c96bd7c66eba54d84c`
- Scope: Android and iOS production History row renderers; six matched pairs, 12 screenshots.

## Findings and disposition

**The requested presentation is confirmed on both platforms.** Failed transactions use a muted X in
the existing neutral icon circle. Their primary amounts are unsigned and use the exact same semantic
color as pending amounts: iOS `.secondary`, Android `onSurfaceVariant`. There is no visible “Failed”
label and no third line. Failure is distinguished by the X rather than amount color.

Completed and pending controls keep their directional arrows and previous amount treatment. Completed
incoming amounts remain green with `+`; completed outgoing remains primary; pending remains secondary.
The standard title/date layout and failed/completed row heights are preserved. The containing row
continues to announce failed status to accessibility; the X is decorative to avoid repeating that status.

No introduced blocking rendering defect was observed in the captured light, dark, or enlarged-text
conditions. **Visual disposition: ready, subject to hosted CI on this exact head.** This review replaces
the earlier red-amount screenshots. The earlier red status-label contrast finding refers to a removed
label; no custom red failure amount or status text remains.

## Routing

| Platform | Decision | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Android | Captured | TransactionRow failure glyph and amount styling changed |
| iOS | Captured | History row icon selection and shared amount styling changed |

No deployment target or version-gated UI path changed, so no additional runtime boundary was needed.

## Capture environments

| Platform | Runtime | Device and viewport | Appearance and text |
|---|---|---|---|
| Android | Android 17 / API 37, CE2A.260420.019, incremental 15611780, security patch 2026-05-05, arm64-v8a | Pixel 8 profile, 1080×2400, 420 dpi, 411.43×914.29 dp | Light/dark at 1.0; light at font scale 1.6; en-US |
| iOS | iOS 26.5 / 23F77; Xcode 26.6 / 17F113 | iPhone 17 Pro, 1206×2622, 402×874 pt, 3× | Light/dark at Dynamic Type Large; light at Accessibility Medium; en-US |

Runtime policy: [Android 17](https://developer.android.com/about/versions/17) is installed. The user
previously approved installed iOS 26.5 as a fallback because the [released iOS 27](https://www.apple.com/newsroom/2026/09/major-updates-for-apples-software-platforms-are-now-available/)
runtime is absent. Each before/after pair uses the same exact guest image and device profile; iOS 27
is not covered. Android captures use a dedicated read-only emulator instance.

## Fixture and build disclosure

Both detached revisions were built independently. Temporary debug-only harnesses call the production
row renderers: HistoryView.transactionRow on iOS and TransactionRow with the production title helper
on Android. The harness does not implement the failure glyph or amount styling. Separate iOS Derived
Data and per-worktree Android builds were used. Executable/APK SHA-256 receipts are in the manifest.

The five synthetic Lightning transactions are, top to bottom: failed outgoing, completed outgoing,
failed incoming, completed incoming, pending outgoing. Each uses 2,100 sat, a fixed 2026-09-07 date,
English, sat-unit display, and no fiat conversion. No real seed, wallet, key, identity, mint, invoice,
token, balance, or payment is included. Capture tests assert fixture readiness and row counts.

Separately, 20 Android tests passed after integrating current main, covering reconciliation, receipt
journeys, the failure X, exact pending-color equality in light/dark, accessible status, absence of a
visible status label, and unchanged row height. Nine selected iOS tests passed, including X selection
for both directions, unchanged arrow controls, History behavior, row height, accessibility status,
and receipt states. No real payment was initiated.

## Cross-platform parity

| Surface | Android | iOS | Classification |
|---|---|---|---|
| Failed transactions | Native Close/X in neutral circle; pending-colored unsigned amount | Native xmark in neutral circle; pending-colored unsigned amount | Requested parity achieved |
| Normal row shape | Two title/date lines, no failure label | Same | No introduced divergence |
| Secondary ink | Native Android pending palette | Native iOS pending palette | Pre-existing palette difference; failed matches pending within each app |
| Enlarged completed incoming amount | Full +2,100 sat with clipped title | Unit may truncate as +2,100 s… with ellipsized title | Pre-existing at the respective enlarged native text settings |
| Row typography and metrics | 40 dp circle; native Android spacing and clipping | 36 pt circle; native iOS spacing and ellipsis | Pre-existing native styling; glyph shape follows each native icon system |

## Limitations and visual noise

- Component captures exercise the real row branches but do not show full History navigation, filters, scrolling, swipe actions, or receipt presentation. Native behavior tests are separate evidence.
- One phone profile per platform. No tablet, landscape, increased contrast, alternate locale/currency, fiat conversion, or physical device capture.
- Enlarged text uses Android 1.6 and iOS Accessibility Medium (approximately 28/17 body scaling). Native typography is comparable, not pixel-identical.
- iOS status bar is fixed at 9:41; Android captures the Compose root without system chrome. Headers and hosting margins are capture-harness chrome, not app navigation changes.
- Screenshots do not prove Lightning settlement, screen-reader speech, secure storage, background behavior, or hardware features.
- Temporary fixture edits were removed from both isolated worktrees. The active source checkout has no uncommitted changes after the implementation and merge commits.

Fixed the Android deposit recovery test setup in 62d19c97.

The test added mints on the instrumentation thread while background restore/balance updates published mint state on the main thread. These concurrent read/modify/write operations could replace the three-mint list with an older two-mint list. The setup now uses `Dispatchers.Main`, matching the production Add Mint screen.

All existing picker assertions remain. Added assertions also verify that all three mints remain in both wallet state and storage after cancelling recovery. No retries or sleeps were added.

Validation on the same API 35 managed-device configuration used by CI:

- 11 selected tests passed: deposit recovery, received-account reconciliation, and failed History row presentation.
- Four additional fresh runs of both deposit recovery tests passed (8 further test executions).
- `git diff --check` passed.

This commit changes Android test code only; the UI and published screenshots are unchanged. Hosted CI is running again. The separate iOS lifecycle failure remains unresolved by this commit.

Investigated the latest iOS failure and the earlier attempt of the same workflow.

- The latest failure was `ActivityDetailUITests.testReceiptLayoutAndVisiblePaymentCode`, waiting for the Received Bitcoin receipt to dismiss. The CI screenshot and accessibility hierarchy confirm that the receipt remained open after the test's slow navigation-title drag.
- The first attempt also read the old on-chain status immediately after tapping Next. Its separate live-payment settlement timeout passed on rerun, as did the earlier wallet-restore lifecycle failure.

This change makes the receipt tests drag the native Sheet Grabber with an explicit fast velocity and still assert that the receipt disappears. It also waits for the exact expected on-chain accessibility value before asserting its text, height, and retry behavior. Existing receipt, QR, and failure-status assertions remain; no test retries or sleeps were added.

Only iOS UI test code changes. Product UI and published screenshots are unchanged.

Pushed as `1f59f6ac`. Validation: all four affected journeys passed three consecutive iterations each (12 successful test executions), including 30 receipt-gallery dismissals; `git diff --check` also passed. Tested with the installed iOS 26.5 simulator. CI uses iOS 26.2; the original gallery test passed once locally before the change, so local testing does not reproduce that exact CI/runtime failure. Hosted CI is running again and must confirm the fix.

Pushed `2f542760` + `77214101`: a follow-up to the Android Send sheet growth.

With the keyboard still open when a destination resolves (typing a Lightning address, which resolves before you put the keyboard away), the first version rose, dropped by ~320 px and rose again. The Material sheet pads its content by the IME inset, so the full-height column grew a second time as the keyboard left and the animated height lagged behind it. The Send flow now passes its sheet insets without the IME (`CashuModalBottomSheet` gained a `contentWindowInsets` parameter; the input face and the connect-mint URL form pad for the keyboard themselves) and hides the keyboard the moment the input face leaves, so the growth is one motion with the keyboard sliding down beside it.

| Lightning address, keyboard open: first version | keyboard-blind version |
| --- | --- |
| ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/swedishfrenchpress/wallet/qa/layout-jump-audit/docs/qa/layout-jump-audit-2026-10-21/img/pixel-send-lnaddress-keyboard-dip-strip.jpg) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/swedishfrenchpress/wallet/qa/layout-jump-audit/docs/qa/layout-jump-audit-2026-10-21/img/fixed-pixel-send-lnaddress-keyboard-strip.jpg) |

Android unit tests (808), screenshot validation and lint pass on this revision. The test plan (`TESTING.md`, scenario 1) now covers the keyboard-open path and the connect-mint form inside Send.

iOS unit target: 726 passed, 43 skipped, 32 failed without the local mint stack (CDK/Nutshell integration classes); re-running those four classes against the local mints now, result to follow.

iOS unit target result on `77214101`: with the local mint stack up (CDK, Nutshell, payment fixtures and the receipt-recovery proxy), every class passes: 726 passed and 43 skipped without the mints, plus the 77 integration tests that need them (76 passed, 1 skipped). The 32 earlier failures were all the missing-mint classes; none is related to this change.

Pushed `90b2a50e`: the Send sheet's back path (amount face → input) started late and kept sinking after the input face had landed. Two nested size animations were chasing each other: `TwoFaceScreen`'s default `SizeTransform` spring and the "To" row's own height animation kept retargeting the sheet's `animateContentSize`. The face container now snaps its size (the host owns the height), the "To" row changes layout in the same frame as the step and only fades, and the sheet height runs the same 300 ms shared-axis curve as the faces. Measured on the Pixel 7a: the sheet moves on the first frame after the tap and settles with the faces at ~280 ms in both directions. Android unit tests (808), screenshot validation and lint pass; `TESTING.md` scenario 2 updated.
a small one. would appreciate your review @asmogo

**Second pass: ecash and transfer, now stacked on #404.** The branch merges `feat/mint-transfer-capability` (`3d7aa601`), so this PR now shows the transfer commits as well; the two new commits on top are `1d583432` (fixes) and `fa051639` (report + test plan). Report section 9 and `TESTING.md` scenarios 8a–8c and 13–16 cover the new ground: Send Ecash (generate, copy, claimed), Receive → paste → claim page → received, Receive Lightning through the mint picker, and the whole Transfer flow on both platforms. Ten more findings, all with fixes: | | | | |---|---|---| | A12 | Android · Send Ecash | "Checking…" row dropped outright, rows below hop 36 dp | | A13 | Android · Receive | sheet jumps 290 dp to the top in one frame before the keyboard moves | | A14 | Android · Receive | token field grows a line at a time | | A15 | Android · Receive/Send → claim page | keyboard outlives the sheet by ~1 s, then vanishes in one frame | | A16 | Android · Transfer | header chevron pops in/out on Continue/Back | | I7 / I8 | iOS · Send Ecash | token face and "Claimed" face land as cuts | | I9 | iOS · Receive Lightning | I3's invoice landing cuts again on the merged branch (and the paid face on an instant mint) | | I10 | iOS · Add mint | keyboard dropped in one frame while the sheet stays | | I11 | iOS · Receive Lightning | QR greys for one frame when a status poll replaces the quote | The iOS ones share a cause worth knowing about: `sendTokens`, `createMintQuote` and the claim/status checks publish wallet state right before they return, so a `withAnimation` landing in that same run-loop pass renders as a cut. Wrapping alone was not enough (measured); the landings now hop to the next pass first. Transfer itself reads cleanly on both platforms (swap, Max, review, commit, success, back): the chevron pop was its only blemish. iOS, before → after (Send Ecash token face; Receive invoice on the merged branch): **Still to come:** the Pixel 7a filmstrips for A12–A16. The recordings were taken and measured, but the machine rebooted before the strips were cut and the recordings did not survive. A13 and A15 were re-recorded on the fixed build before that and scan as animated; A12, A14 and A16 are marked "fix applied" in the report until the hardware re-check. Android unit tests, screenshot validation and lint pass on the merged branch with the fixes. iOS unit target on the simulator: 893 tests, 871 passed, 0 failed, 22 skipped (local mint fixtures). Side finding, not in scope here: on the Pixel the Send Ecash face never reported a token as claimed although a second wallet redeemed it within a minute (iOS reports it in about six seconds). Worth a separate look at the Android claim probe. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

**Pixel 7a before/after for the second pass is in** (`c19933a9`, `9f0402f3`). Every Android finding was recorded twice with the same script: the merged branch without the fixes, then the fixed build. All five are now verified on hardware; report section 9 has the strips and numbers. One more fix came out of it: animating the sheet column alone (first attempt) eased the sheet's edge while the rows under the token field still hopped a line at a time. The size animation now sits on the Receive and Send destination fields themselves, and the wrap spreads over ~15 frames. A13 Receive sheet on keyboard open, before → after: A15 token handoff (keyboard lingering, then cut), before → after: A14 token wrap, before → after: A12 "Checking…" row and A16 Transfer chevron, after: Also swept on both platforms with nothing to report: Receive → Ecash (new Cashu request page), Send → Tap (Android), Send → paste a token → claim page, Send → Lightning address with the field animation in place, Transfer end to end. One item is left open and documented (I12): the iOS compact Send/Receive sheet steps ~27 pt in one frame when a four-line token is pasted. SwiftUI does not animate a changed `.height` detent even inside `withAnimation` (tried, measured, reverted); the sheet leaves for the claim page within a second, so it is brief. Checks: Android unit tests, screenshot validation and lint pass after the field change; iOS unit target 893 / 871 passed / 0 failed / 22 skipped; no test files changed. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
